 New capital gains tax brackets for 2027
 Andrew Dorn Mon, November 9, 2026 at 5:44 PM CST 2 min read ( NewsNation ) — The IRS' new tax brackets for long-term capital gains could let you keep more of your investment profits in 2027. 
 For single filers, the 0% rate on long-term capital gains will apply to taxable income up to $51,050, up from $49,450 in 2026. For married couples filing jointly, the cutoff is rising from $98,900 to $102,100. 
  New tax brackets and standard deductions for 2027  
 Those increases could lower your tax bill if you sell a stock after holding it for more than a year. Any profit from the sale generally counts as a long-term capital gain, but the amount you owe depends on your income and filing status. 
  7 key tax terms you should know  
 Most long-term capital gains are taxed at 0%, 15% or 20%, with higher rates kicking in as income rises. 
 Short-term capital gains, profits from assets held for a year or less, are taxed as ordinary income. The cutoffs for those tax brackets are also rising in 2027. 
 The new income thresholds apply to tax year 2027, meaning the changes will affect investments you sell for a gain during the next calendar year.
